title: 2005 AMC 12B Problem 19
statement: Let \(x\) and \(y\) be two-digit integers such that \(y\) is obtained by reversing the digits of \(x.\) The integers \(x\) and \(y\) satisfy \(x^2 - y^2 = m^2\) for some positive integer \(m.\) What is \(x + y + m?\)

solutions.text:
Let \(x = 10a + b\) and \(y = 10b + a\) with \(a \gt b.\) Then \[ \begin{aligned} &x^2 - y^2 = (10a+b)^2 \\ &\quad {}- (10b+a)^2 \\ &= 99(a^2 - b^2) \\ &= 99(a+b)(a-b). \end{aligned} \]

Since \(99 = 9 \cdot 11,\) for this to be a perfect square we need \((a+b)(a-b)\) to be a multiple of \(11.\) As \(a + b \le 17\) and \(a - b \le 8,\) the only multiple of \(11\) available is \(a + b = 11.\)

Then \(x^2 - y^2 = 9 \cdot 11^2 (a - b),\) which is a perfect square exactly when \(a - b\) is a perfect square. Because \(a+b=11\) is odd, \(a-b\) is odd; and because \(1 \le a-b \le 8,\) its only possible square value is \(1.\) Hence \((a, b) = (6, 5).\)

So \(x = 65,\) \(y = 56,\) and \(m = \sqrt{65^2 - 56^2}\) \(= \sqrt{1089} = 33.\) Thus \(x + y + m\) \(= 65 + 56 + 33 = 154.\)

Thus, the correct answer is E.
hints: For \(99(a-b)(a+b)\) to be a perfect square, \(a+b\) must be \(11\)
